title: Keep the final spill when a mixed merge cannot protect downstream admission
question: Can a final retained batch improve hosted Uniform without taking shared memory needed by the decoder and writer?
summary: The mixed merge saves 22.7 MB each way in tracked temporary traffic and 0.127 seconds at the paired median. Under a matched late WASI peer grant it fails before the first decoded row while the ordinary spill encodes all 13.

workloads: 150,003 rows with one existing disk run and a final batch, plus a resident control.

validation.summary: Complete export conservation and caps, exact pinned key order, early shared pressure fallback, late peer counterexample, cancellation and cleanup.

limitations: Shared pressure coverage uses injected peer grants within one WASI or native ledger. Three complete pairs on one WSL2 host.
exclusions: More than one disk run in the hosted timing cell, physical device I/O, native elapsed time and delivery of the prototype.
reopen_when: A bounded mixed cursor can retain its batch while securing decode and encoder capacity through the matched late peer control.
